overview: Wipro is a Bengaluru-headquartered, 80-year-old IT services and consulting company that helps enterprises with digital transformation, cloud, engineering, consulting and AI-powered solutions, delivered through a global offshore/onsite delivery model. It serves 1,233+ active clients across Americas, Europe and APMEA through four Strategic Market Units, organized around industry verticals (BFSI, Consumer, Technology & Communications, Energy/Manufacturing/Resources, and Health). Wipro is dual-listed, trading as WIPRO on the NSE/BSE in India and as an ADR (WIT) on the NYSE, though this analysis covers the India-listed entity.

business_model.summary: Wipro earns revenue by billing enterprise clients for IT services on a time-and-materials, fixed-price-project, or managed-services basis, supplemented by consulting (Capco, Designit) and business process services (BPS). Revenue is largely non-recurring project/staff-augmentation work with a growing base of multi-year managed-services and large deal contracts (e.g., the ~$1B, 8-year Olam Group transformation deal) that add a more annuity-like layer.
business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise and government; 1,233 active global clients, 18 clients >$100M and 45 clients >$50M in trailing-12-month revenue; top customer concentration only 4.5-4.6% of revenue, top 10 customers ~24%
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas 1: 34.4%, Americas 2 (Latin America): 25.6% [note: SMU split differs from revenue-by-region], Europe: 27.4%, APMEA (Asia Pacific, Middle East & Africa): 12.6%; Offshore revenue 62.2% vs. Onsite revenue 37.8%

competitive_position.market_position: Wipro is one of India's top-4 IT services exporters (alongside TCS, Infosys and HCLTech) with FY26 IT services revenue of roughly $11.2bn, but it is smaller and has grown more slowly than TCS and Infosys in recent years, and is dwarfed in scale by Accenture (~$71bn revenue). It is positioned as a full-stack 'consulting-led, AI-powered' player after folding in Capco (BFSI consulting) and Designit (design) and is now adding Mindsprint (enterprise GCC/shared-services capability).

moat_factors.description: Long-tenured enterprise relationships and embedded, mission-critical systems create multi-year contracts and high re-papering/transition costs for clients
240K+ employees across 65 countries and six continents support large, geographically distributed delivery, though scale trails TCS, Infosys and Accenture
Capco (banking/capital markets consulting) and Designit (design) give Wipro higher-value, less commoditized entry points than pure staff augmentation
India-based offshore delivery (62% of revenue) still underpins cost competitiveness, but this is the exact lever GenAI/automation threatens to compress
97.3% of FY26 revenue came from existing customers, reflecting sticky, repeat-business relationships, though this also signals limited new-logo momentum

weaknesses: Persistent growth laggard versus TCS, Infosys and HCLTech over multiple years, with IT services revenue roughly flat to low-single-digit in constant currency
High exposure to BFSI (34.5% of revenue), making results sensitive to bank/financial-sector IT budget cycles
Weak large-deal bookings momentum recently (large deal TCV down 58.6% QoQ in Q2 FY27), signalling demand softness or pricing pressure
Lower margin profile than best-in-class peers, with management explicitly trading near-term margin for AI/engineering investment
Smaller scale than Accenture and TCS limits ability to absorb pricing pressure or fund large AI platform investment at the same pace

growth_drivers: Wipro Intelligence (TM) — unified suite of AI-powered platforms and agentic/GenAI offerings being cross-sold into the existing client base
Large, multi-year transformation deals such as the ~$1B+ (committed spend ~$800M), 8-year Olam Group engagement
Bolt-on M&A to add capability: Mindsprint acquisition ($375M, enterprise shared-services/GCC capability), Alpha Net Consulting contract acquisition (~$70.8M, AI-powered application services)
Consulting-led positioning via Capco (BFSI) and Designit (design/CX) to move up the value chain from staff augmentation

Five strategic priorities: building large accounts in prioritized sectors, winning large deals with a consulting-led/AI approach, differentiating via Wipro Intelligence, scaling AI-skilled talent, and deepening client-centric delivery
GCC (Global Capability Center) advisory/build work as multinationals set up their own India captives
Capital return program (buybacks and dividends) supporting EPS growth even where revenue growth is modest

business.risk: GenAI disruption to the services/labor-arbitrage model
business.description: Brokerages estimate up to ~15% of IT services revenue at risk as AI compresses billable effort; labor arbitrage reportedly drives 22-45% of major IT firms' revenue, and clients are demanding AI-productivity discounts
Total bookings fell 22.9% QoQ and large deal TCV fell 58.6% QoQ in Q2 FY27 (constant currency), a leading indicator for future revenue
BFSI is 34.5% of revenue; a slowdown in bank/financial-services IT spending would disproportionately hit Wipro
TCS, Infosys, HCLTech and Accenture all compete for the same large-deal pipeline, pressuring pricing and win rates
Voluntary attrition running at 13.8% (TTM); retaining AI/consulting talent is both a cost and execution risk

financial.description: Revenue is earned in USD, GBP, EUR, AUD and CAD but reported in INR; guidance is explicitly built on assumed FX rates (e.g., USD/INR ~95.76, EUR/USD 1.15), and INR depreciation/appreciation swings reported growth
Multiple recent acquisitions (Capco, Designit, Mindsprint, Alpha Net contracts) raise integration and goodwill risk, and management has flagged near-term margin headwinds from these investments

The FY26 Rs 15,000 crore (~Rs150.5bn) tender buyback at Rs250/share reduced cash and investments materially (cash fell from ~Rs26.8bn to ~Rs15.3bn at the holding company level between March and September 2026)

regulatory.description: US visa policy (H-1B), data localization rules in client geographies, and India labor-code changes (e.g., gratuity/leave-encashment remeasurement cited in FY26 results) affect cost structure and delivery model
As a dual-listed company (NSE/BSE and NYSE ADR), Wipro must satisfy both SEBI LODR and SEC requirements, adding compliance overhead

macro.description: IT services demand is tied to enterprise discretionary tech budgets, which contract in a global slowdown; Q3 FY27 (Dec-2026 quarter) guidance of -1.5% to +0.5% QoQ in constant currency signals a soft near-term demand backdrop
Higher-for-longer rates in the US/Europe can delay large transformation deals and extend sales cycles among BFSI and other discretionary-spend clients

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global IT services/outsourcing spending is expected to grow only modestly in the near term as enterprises redirect budgets toward AI initiatives and away from traditional staff-augmentation work; GenAI is reshaping both demand (new AI-delivery work) and the cost base (automation of lower-value tasks)
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high — enterprise IT services spend is discretionary and tends to lag/lead broader corporate capex and bank/financial-sector budget cycles; large-deal signing activity is an early cyclical indicator
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity — higher rates slow client capex and can delay large multi-year transformation deals, particularly in BFSI
key_input_costs: Data center/cloud infrastructure costs for AI delivery platforms

recent_developments.event: Q2 FY27 results: IT services revenue flat QoQ / +0.6% YoY in constant currency; operating margin improved to 16.5% (+50bps QoQ); net income down ~1.9-4.7% depending on basis; total bookings fell 22.9% QoQ and large deal TCV fell 58.6% QoQ in constant currency; stock/ADR fell on the soft Q3 FY27 guidance

Management (CEO Srini Pallia) guided Q3 FY27 (quarter ending Dec 31, 2026) IT services revenue of $2,571M-$2,625M, implying -1.5% to +0.5% QoQ in constant currency, and said Wipro will keep investing in AI/engineering capability even where it pressures near-term margins

Completed Rs15,000 crore (Rs150.5bn including costs) tender-offer buyback of 600 million equity shares at Rs250/share (~5.7% of paid-up capital), settled June 24, 2026, shares extinguished June 25, 2026

Signed an ~$1B+ (committed spend ~$800M), 8-year strategic transformation deal with Singapore's Olam Group, and a definitive agreement to acquire Olam's Mindsprint shared-services/GCC business for $375 million
Acquired select customer contracts from Alpha Net Consulting for up to $70.8 million to bolster AI-powered application services and consulting capabilities
FY2026 (year ended March 31, 2026) consolidated revenue ~Rs926.2bn (Ind AS) with profit for the year of Rs132.7bn; voluntary attrition stood at 13.8% TTM and headcount exceeded 240,000

Srini Pallia continues as CEO (succeeded Thierry Delaporte), with the company's strategy organized around five pillars: consulting-led, AI-powered, industry-focused, client-centric and purpose-driven, unified under the 'Wipro Intelligence' platform brand

items.notes: Implies -1.5% to +0.5% QoQ in constant currency; guidance assumes GBP/USD 1.35, EUR/USD 1.15, AUD/USD 0.71, USD/INR 95.76, CAD/USD 0.72; the market read this as disappointing given weak Q2 bookings

items.target: No explicit numeric target disclosed; management signaled willingness to accept near-term compression
items.notes: CEO Srini Pallia said Wipro will continue investing in AI, engineering and acquisitions 'even when they create near-term margin headwinds'; Q2 FY27 operating margin was 16.5%

items.target: No numeric forward target disclosed in the reviewed materials
items.notes: Management flagged that some confirmed Q2 orders were delayed by unsigned paperwork and are expected to close in Q3 FY27, implying a bookings catch-up rather than a change in underlying demand

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Srini Pallia characterized the demand environment as 'largely unchanged' and reiterated commitment to investing through AI, engineering capability and M&A despite near-term margin pressure. The sharp sequential drop in bookings and large-deal TCV was attributed partly to deal-signing timing (paperwork delays) rather than solely to demand deterioration, though analysts remained skeptical, citing the stock/ADR reaction to the guidance.

bull_case: Low customer concentration (top customer ~4.5% of revenue) and diversified sector mix reduce single-client/sector risk versus some peers
Consulting-led acquisitions (Capco, Designit) and the new Mindsprint/GCC capability move Wipro up the value chain away from pure commoditized staff augmentation
Large, multi-year anchor deals like the Olam Group transformation contract provide revenue visibility and showcase Wipro's ability to win big-ticket AI-led transformation work
Active capital return program (buybacks plus dividends) supports EPS and ROE even in a period of muted top-line growth

Management is explicitly reinvesting (rather than harvesting margin) into AI/engineering capability, which could position Wipro better than slower-moving peers if GenAI-native services become the next growth vector
bear_case: GenAI-driven compression of labor-arbitrage economics directly threatens Wipro's core offshore delivery model, with analyst estimates of up to 15% of industry revenue at risk
Bookings momentum has deteriorated sharply (total bookings -22.9% QoQ, large deal TCV -58.6% QoQ), a leading indicator that near-term revenue growth could stay weak or negative
Wipro has persistently grown slower than TCS, Infosys and HCLTech over multiple years, suggesting a structural share-loss or execution issue rather than a one-off soft quarter
Heavy BFSI exposure (34.5% of revenue) leaves Wipro vulnerable to any slowdown in bank/financial-services technology budgets

Sell-side sentiment has been negative into late 2026 (Goldman Sachs and Citi maintaining Sell ratings, Morgan Stanley and CLSA downgrades earlier in the year), reflecting skepticism about the growth and margin trajectory
